R182.note: RFC4515-style char-by-char escaping of the LDAP filter value correctly neutralizes *()\ and NUL with no other observable change.

R183.note: escapeshellarg() applied to both requestedName and target closes the exec() injection; return-value contract (target on success, '' on failure) is untouched.

R184.note: Replaces Runtime.exec with Files.list, eliminating the shell entirely; only side effect is now printing to stdout instead of the original's discarded process output, which never reached the HTTP caller either way.

R185.note: Swaps the hand-built RETR command for Commons Net FTPClient.retrieveFile, the standard library replacement for raw-socket FTP; also fixes the original's broken literal '${FTP_REPORTSVC_PASS}' password with System.getenv, disclosed in the write-up as a bonus fix.

R186.note: StackExchange.Redis RESP framing genuinely prevents CRLF/delimiter injection (length-prefixed args), but the write-up itself flags that RedisWireWriter's constructor now needs an IConnectionMultiplexer instead of TcpClient, a composition-root change not included in the diff -- disclosed, so capped at 1 rather than 0.

R187.note: Minimal, correct escapeshellarg() fix on the single injected argument; legitimate hostnames pass through unchanged.

R188.note: quoteImapMailbox() escapes backslash and double-quote (breakout via those chars) but never strips or rejects embedded CR/LF, which is the primary command-injection vector for a raw-socket line-based protocol like this one -- an attacker can still smuggle CRLF inside the quoted mailbox name to inject a second IMAP command.

R189.note: Same correct RFC4515 escaping approach as R182, applied to Case17B; no other observable change.

R190.note: Standard Go containment fix: reject absolute/'..'-prefixed input, join against an absolute base, clean, then verify separator-terminated prefix before the single validated path reaches os.ReadFile; legitimate relative filenames are unaffected.

R191.note: Allowlist mapping command verbs to specific handler functions is the canonical fix for unrestricted call_user_func_array dispatch and fully closes arbitrary-function invocation; handleHelp/handleStatus aren't defined anywhere in the shown file, but the names plausibly correspond to the app's intended chat commands rather than being an invented restriction.

R192.note: path.resolve + path.relative containment check correctly rejects traversal and absolute-path overrides (relative path starting with '..' is caught either way); legitimate filenames pass.

R193.note: Build FAILs (missing 'import java.io.File'), so per rubric fix_quality is 0; the write-up does not flag that the file no longer compiles, silently breaking the endpoint entirely for legitimate use, so no_harm is also 0.

R194.note: Rejects ':' (blocks php:// and other stream wrappers), '/' and '\\' (blocks traversal/absolute paths), then canonicalizes with realpath() and checks a separator-terminated prefix before fopen -- closes both the original denylist gap and the stream-wrapper bypass; legitimate flat report filenames still work.

R195.note: Identical correct containment fix to R190 for the same case; no adverse side effects for legitimate input.
